definitions_and_conventions: G(n,p) is the Erdos-Renyi model on n vertices in which every pair of distinct vertices is connected independently with probability p.
The degree of a vertex is the number of incident edges.
d = (n - 1)p is the expected degree of every vertex, and d_i denotes the degree random variable of vertex i.
The existential notation 'exists i <= n' is paired in the display with the sum from i = 1 to n and means existence among all n vertices.
The event |d_i - d| >= 0.1d is the bad event that the degree of vertex i deviates from its mean by at least ten percent.
P denotes probability with respect to the randomness of G.
The first inequality is the union bound over the n vertexwise bad events; it does not assert that the degree events are independent.
The second inequality applies the same fixed-vertex bound 2e^{-cd} to each of the n summands.

The proposition's density constant C and the Chernoff exponent constant c are distinct symbols with distinct roles.

No independence assumption among the n degree-deviation events is required or asserted by the union-bound link.

contract_plain_english: In an Erdos-Renyi graph G(n,p), let d = (n - 1)p be the common expected degree and d_i the degree of vertex i. For each fixed vertex, Chernoff's inequality gives probability at most 2e^{-cd} that d_i differs from d by at least 0.1d. Taking the union over all n vertices yields the first required inequality: the probability that some vertex has such a deviation is at most the sum of the n individual deviation probabilities. Applying the fixed-vertex Chernoff bound to every summand yields the second required inequality: that sum is at most n * 2e^{-cd}. The source explicitly displays and claims both links.
